challengeFindings.title: A code step whose `bkit:generate` fails (a FAIL verdict with its `BLOCKED — bkit:generate` line, or a HANDOVER mid-edit) now exits 16, which no workflow routes, so a step that used to land and enter the remediate or handover loop sends the whole build to the Failure Path

A code step whose engine change adds a seeded `bkit.workflows` default is refused with exit 13 on every finish, because this repo's `bkit:generate` runs `pnpm bkit upgrade` (`seedBkitDefaults` writes every missing seeded key into `package.json`) before the `bkit.workflows` check, so restoring HEAD's values as the exit-13 message says is undone by the next finish's generate

Finish runs `bkit:generate` before it stages the code step's edits, so this repo's last generate link `bkit:graph:refresh` (which rebuilds `docs/capabilities.md` from `git write-tree`, the index) builds the register from the pre-edit tree, and the code step's commit carries a stale register that the pre-push register gate refuses later

A `bkit:generate` killed by a signal (the out-of-memory killer, a host timeout) is logged as `pnpm bkit:generate exited undefined`, because `spawnSync` then sets `status` null and `signal`, not `error`, and the message reads only `res.status ?? res.error?.message`

challengeFindings.title: In bkit's own repo, the round-1 refusal this group set out to fix still ends the run: a code step that follows its prompt runs `pnpm bkit:generate` itself (`.bkit/core/prompts/bkit-build-plan-tasks.md:121`, `.bkit/core/prompts/bkit-build-plan-gaps-remediate.md:106`), whose `pnpm bkit upgrade` writes the new seeded `bkit.workflows` key into `package.json` (`upgrade.ts:941` → `modules/index.ts:159` → `core.ts:591` `seedBkitDefaults`) before finish takes its "before generate" reading, so the first finish exits 13 as "the step's own edit"; a key left by a finish the hook (exit 8) or the planned-test lock (exit 11) refused does the same on the re-run; no build step routes exit 13, so the run goes to the Failure Path

A failed `bkit:generate` at a code step's finish is recorded as one more "a code step edited a planned test case" in any repo whose `.bkit/friction.jsonl` already holds an exit-11 row for that step (this repo does, at `recurrenceCount` 7), because `recordGenerateFriction` and `recordTestLockFriction` both key their rows `steps-finish/<step>` and `appendFrictionRow` folds a same-key row into the prior row's summary and description, so the only durable record of a step that landed with stale generated output is lost

A step that leaves `package.json` unparseable (a trailing comma after a script edit) is now refused with exit 13 as "the step's own edit changes bkit.workflows" for every key HEAD holds, which no build step routes, where it used to skip the check and reach the commit, whose hook refusal (exit 8) the build routes back to a fix; `readWorkflows` returns `{}` for an unreadable file, so a parse failure reads as every key removed

`b771d80fd` switched the three install call sites (`syncPayloadLinks`, `syncTemplateCopies`, `warnMissingLintStagedConfig`) from `path.resolve(cwd) === getPkgRoot()` to `isBkitOwnRepo(cwd)`, so `bkit upgrade` in a linked worktree of a bkit checkout run with the main checkout's engine, or in a non-git folder inside that checkout, now skips the template copies, the payload links and the lint-staged warning; the owner's ruling covered only the `bkit.workflows` check, no test pins the new install behaviour, and `bkit uninstall` in the same worktree still uses the old check, so it deletes `.bkit/templates/` whole while install and upgrade call it bkit's own source

Running `bkit install` or `bkit upgrade` with bkit's main-checkout engine on a non-git folder inside that checkout (a scratch consumer at `tmp/scratch`) now classes the folder as bkit's own repository, so install writes the rest of the payload there but silently skips the `.bkit/templates/` copies, the `.bkit/core` / `.bkit/shared` view links and the lint-staged warning
